target_definition: Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. KNHANES reports physician-diagnosed hypertension without confirming essential versus secondary hypertension.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. KNHANES dyslipidaemia is broader than pure hypercholesterolaemia. Must not label this as an exact hypercholesterolaemia validation.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. The physician-diagnosis question does not distinguish type 1, type 2, or gestational diabetes. Do not infer type from insulin use or age.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. KNHANES asks kidney disease without establishing duration or CKD stage; eGFR threshold is not used to manufacture a target label.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. Physician-diagnosed asthma lacks the UKB main-diagnosis restriction and expanded control exclusions. In 2024 children also answer; the analysis remains age 40–70.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. Self-reported physician-diagnosed stroke is not subtype-resolved; 2022 and 2023 do not contain this respondent diagnosis field.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. MI/angina is narrower than all I20–I25 ischaemic heart disease. Use official DI4_dg 0/1 and audit against DI5_dg and DI6_dg; do not convert unknown components to 0.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. Use physician diagnosis, not DX_OST or T-score thresholds. Both sexes are eligible; the diagnosis question is adult-wide even though DXA measurement has a separate age restriction.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. The question specifically requires a physician diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnoea through sleep testing in hospital or at home; UKB G47.3 sleep apnoea is broader. Absent in 2024.

Cross-sectional reported physician diagnosis; not incident disease prediction. Spirometry questionnaire asks diagnosed COPD including chronic bronchitis/emphysema; this is not the UKB ICD-mode construction. Do not use HE_COPD1 (FEV1/FVC-defined obstruction).
